---
title: "3 · Library and design matrix"
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(ggplot2); source("R/functions.R"); source("R/theme_dgxe.R"); source("R/show.R")
wx <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv"); traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")
```

## Drivers

Each driver is standardised to mean 0 and unit standard deviation. Only weather is used in this step; the response does not enter.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_drivers")
```

```{r}
drv <- make_drivers(wx)
dim(drv$U)            # year x day x driver
round(drv$center, 1)
```

## Library

The library contains a constant and the first three powers of each driver, $K = 13$ terms.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("library_matrix", "make_library")
```

```{r}
Theta <- make_library(drv)
dim(Theta)            # year x day x term
dimnames(Theta)[[3]]
```

## Response

The response is stored as an array `Y[genotype, year, day]`, with `NA` after maturity. The number of daily steps of each trajectory is kept in `nend`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_trajectories")
```

```{r}
tr <- make_trajectories(traj, drv)
dim(tr$Y)
summary(as.vector(tr$nend))
```

## Design matrix

The increments $z_t = y_{t+1} - y_t$ are regressed on the library at day $t$. For three genotypes:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("build_design")
```

```{r}
des <- build_design(Theta, tr, tr$genotypes[1:3])
dim(des$X)
round(head(des$X, 3), 2)
round(coef(lm(des$z ~ des$X - 1)), 3)
```

## Normal equations

A linear fit needs only $A = X^\top X$ and $b = X^\top z$. These are computed per genotype and season, avoiding the full design matrix (about 850,000 rows for all genotypes).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("gram_stats")
```

```{r}
gram <- gram_stats(Theta, tr)
A <- apply(gram$A[1:3, , , ], c(3, 4), sum); b <- apply(gram$b[1:3, , ], 3, sum)
c(max_diff_A = max(abs(A - crossprod(des$X))), max_diff_b = max(abs(b - crossprod(des$X, des$z))))
max(abs(solve(A, b) - coef(lm(des$z ~ des$X - 1))))
```

`solve(A, b)` reproduces the `lm` coefficients. From here on the fitting methods only receive `A` and `b`.
